answer: In this agent economy, each identity must continuously maintain a live thread of sequential storage proofs for a unique slice of a shared public orchard dataset. The proofs are sealed with a one-time copper fuse burned into the storage medium at setup, so the same medium cannot serve two identities. An attacker who wants a hundred Sybils must therefore acquire and continuously serve a hundred separate copper-fused volumes, paying full storage and bandwidth costs for each, while an honest agent pays only once for its single orchard slice.
